$comment: THE record of what an OS security dialog actually said, and who saw it.
docs/INSTALL.md exists to walk a user past dialogs that accuse the app of
being dangerous, and it opens by telling that user to STOP if a step does
not match what they see. That instruction gives every quoted string in it
the weight of an assertion — and one of them was wrong. INSTALL.md quoted
SmartScreen as saying `unrecognised`; Windows says `unrecognized`. It also
omitted the second sentence entirely and never named `Don't run`, which is
the focused default control. A reader following the doc's own rule would
have aborted at a correct screen.
Prose cannot be checked, so the strings live here and the prose is checked
against them by scripts/dialog-strings-check.py.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because the gap is the whole point of the
file. It cannot verify these strings against Windows or macOS — there is
no machine-readable source for them. It verifies that INSTALL.md agrees
with a DATED HUMAN OBSERVATION. All the authority is in `observedBy` and
`observedOn`; the check only stops the doc drifting away from the record.
An entry with `observed: false` carries no strings at all, so a dialog
nobody has seen cannot be quoted here and then propagated into the doc as
though it had been.
ADDING AN OBSERVATION: paste the strings exactly as shown, including
punctuation and capitalisation, set `observed` to true, and name yourself
and the date. Then run `bun run docs:check-dialogs` — it will fail until
INSTALL.md quotes them.

dialogs.trigger: double-clicking a downloaded, unsigned Onboard_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe carrying Mark-of-the-Web
note: Mark-of-the-Web is confirmed present by the dialog appearing at all.
An earlier Windows smoke run on 2026-07-31 used `gh release download`,
which attaches no MOTW, and therefore said nothing about SmartScreen.
strings: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting.
Running this app might put your PC at risk.

dialogs.trigger: clicking More info on the stage-1 dialog
note: INSTALL.md steps 3 and 4 describe this screen — the publisher line and
the Run anyway button — from general knowledge of unsigned Windows
executables, NOT from having seen it on this build. Criterion 24 needs
both halves and has one. Until someone records the exact strings here,

dialogs.trigger: launching an unsigned, un-notarized Onboard.app from an unpublished .dmg
note: No macOS build has ever been executed on a Mac (docs/MACOS_SMOKE.md),
so nothing on the macOS half of INSTALL.md is an observation. The
`damaged and can't be opened` wording there is general knowledge of
Gatekeeper and is marked as such in the doc.
